record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.original_question: Describe finitely generated commutative separative E-semigroups, where an E-semigroup is a commutative semigroup isomorphic to the semigroup of all its endomorphisms under pointwise multiplication.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.7. (A.A. Borisov) Describe finitely generated commutative separative E-semigroups.
It is proved in [5] that for a finitely defined commutative semigroup the problem of deciding whether
the semigroup of all its endomorphisms (under pointwise multiplication) is Archimedean is algo-
rithmically solvable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a commutative semigroup, and let $\operatorname{End}(S)$ denote the set of all semigroup endomorphisms $S \to S$, equipped with the pointwise multiplication operation $(\varphi \cdot \psi)(x) = \varphi(x)\psi(x)$, which makes $\operatorname{End}(S)$ into a commutative semigroup. Call $S$ an $E$-semigroup if there exists a semigroup isomorphism $S \cong \operatorname{End}(S)$. A commutative semigroup $S$ is called separative if for all $a, b \in S$ the equalities $a^2 = ab = b^2$ imply $a = b$.

Give a structural description (classification) of all finitely generated commutative separative $E$-semigroups.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a 2026 collection of unsolved problems in semigroup theory (Lyapin's notebook), listed as an open problem of A.A. Borisov. While Borisov has classified several adjacent classes (finite, idempotent-free, cancellative, and Archimedean finitely generated commutative E-semigroups), no published description of the separative case was found.
